sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Sign in, create or join a household and create a list. Country, currency and language are optional and can be changed later.
Invite family members from Household. Each invitation is for one person’s sign-in email, can be used once, expires after seven days and can be revoked. Each person needs their own account.
Explore the demo to try the app with a browser-only example household. Demo changes never become real household records.

sections.heading: Shared lists
bullets: Type items like “2 kg apples”, “bread x3”, “1.000 g Mehl” or “2 x 1.5 l water”; the quantity, unit and category are suggested for you.
Everyone in the household sees changes within a few seconds. Offline changes are kept on the device and sent in order when you reconnect.
If two people change the same item, both versions are shown so you can choose.
Finish a trip to record what was bought; “Same again” repeats it later.

sections.heading: Search and scan products
paragraphs: Search by name, brand or barcode, or scan a barcode with the camera. The saved Swiss catalogue answers most scans instantly; other products are looked up on Open Food Facts.
bullets: 98,179 products sold in Switzerland can be found by barcode, 85,611 of them with nutrition values.
33,759 products are linked to a retailer: Coop 12,986, Migros 16,831, Denner 1,672, Lidl 1,157, Aldi 685, and a few hundred for Volg, Spar, Manor and Globus.
Retailer links come from community tags and own brands (for example Naturaplan, Prix Garantie, M-Classic, M-Budget). They are not a complete assortment and do not show current stock or prices.
Catalogue data is from the Open Food Facts export of 25 September 2026 (ODbL). Always check the package, especially for allergies.

sections.heading: Health score
paragraphs: Each product page shows a score from 0 to 100 with its breakdown, so you can see exactly why a product scores as it does.
bullets: Nutrition, up to 60 points, from the Nutri-Score grade: A 60, B 48, C 33, D 18, E 5. The grade computed by Open Food Facts is used when available; otherwise it is estimated from the label and marked as an estimate.

Additives, up to 30 points, minus 15, 8 or 3 for each additive with a high, moderate or limited flag. Each flag names its source (EU, EFSA, WHO/IARC). A high flag caps the score at 49. An additive without a flag is not a safety finding.
Organic, 10 points, when a recognised organic label is recorded (EU organic, Bio Suisse, Demeter and others).
Processing level (NOVA 1–4) is shown but not scored.
Products without energy, sugars, saturated fat and salt are shown as “Not scored” instead of guessed.
Scores: 75 and above Excellent, 50–74 Good, 25–49 Mediocre, below 25 Poor. The score compares similar products; it is not medical or allergy advice.

sections.heading: Better alternatives
paragraphs: Under the score, the app suggests products from the same category that score at least 10 points higher. Choose Any Swiss shop, Coop, Migros, Denner, Lidl or Aldi to see only products linked to that retailer. Taste, allergens and current stock are not compared.
For whole lists abroad, Find abroad suggests alternatives for each item and applies your household’s requirements and allergies.

sections.heading: Scan a receipt
paragraphs: Open Lists → Scan receipt, take or upload a photo (or paste the text), adjust the crop and review each row before adding.
bullets: Coop, Migros, Denner, Lidl, Aldi and other receipt layouts are recognised, including weighed items (“0.785 kg x 2.99 CHF/kg”), counts (“2 x 4.95”), multipacks and Aktion or Cumulus discounts.
When a line’s words match a product in the saved catalogue, the row offers “Link this product”. Nothing is linked unless you choose it; linked items get photos, nutrition and a health score.
Text recognition runs on your device. The receipt photo and full text are never uploaded; only the rows you add are shared.
Past receipt prices are kept as history and never become the next shop’s price.

sections.heading: Meals and nutrition
paragraphs: Save recipes with weighed ingredients, plan portions for each person and add ingredients to a list. Daily totals separate planned from eaten portions and show how complete the nutrition data is. Generic ingredients use the Swiss Food Composition Database (FSVO).

sections.heading: Shops, branches and offers
paragraphs: In a shop’s page, search its catalogue, see your list for that shop, record offers you have seen and find nearby branches (OpenStreetMap). Coop, Migros, Denner, Lidl and Aldi are supported in Switzerland, plus Tesco, Carrefour and Walmart abroad.
A nearby supermarket is not proof that a product is in stock, and offers are what household members entered.

sections.heading: Privacy
bullets: Only household members can read or change household data. Photos are private to the household.
Export your data or delete your account from Household. Deleting a household removes its photos.
Signing out clears the household copy on that device.
